surface: The Octane-native surface contains DeleteResource, CommandPalette, Flow, ClipboardText and Toast with Toasty/ToastProvider and Kumo manager helpers, legacy Code and CodeBlock plus isolated code and code/server highlighting subpaths, DatePicker and the deprecated DateRangePicker, Table and Pagination, Badge, Banner, Breadcrumbs, Button, RefreshButton, LinkButton, Loader and SkeletonLine, Tooltip, TooltipProvider, LinkProvider, KumoPortalProvider, Label, Field, Input, InputArea and its Textarea alias, InputGroup, SensitiveInput, Select, Autocomplete, Combobox, Meter, Empty, Text, Link, LayerCard and its deprecated Surface wrapper, Grid and GridItem, CloudflareLogo and PoweredByCloudflare, TableOfContents with its active-id hook, Tabs, Toolbar, the deprecated MenuBar with its navigation hook, the complete Collapsible, Dialog, Popover, DropdownMenu, Checkbox, Sidebar, and Switch families, and the generic Radio family with its direct RadioGroup export. Presence records availability only; Chart, SankeyChart, TimeseriesChart, and primitive subpaths are not yet exported.
divergences: Switch retains semantic fill/interact/brand/contrast tokens rather than the oracle's hard-coded light/dark palette. The compatibility follow-up restores its light off-state fill and removes the inline-baseline wrapper gap; dark and checked colors are not literal palette parity.

Select uses an explicit field-label relationship to avoid Aria's selected-value/self-label duplication. A layout-transparent native event wrapper commits Aria navigation and focuses its roving option before rapid Enter; Aria still owns navigation, selection, initial autofocus and dismissal.

DeleteResource uses native Dialog/Input/Button composition and shared clipboard fallback. Copy success is announced, reset after 1500ms, and ignored after closing/unmounting. Pending onDelete promises guard concurrent activation; loading, errors and dismissal remain caller-owned.

CommandPalette uses @octanejs/aria Autocomplete/SearchField/ListBox because the pinned native Base UI lacks autocomplete. Value-key registration preserves arbitrary items, Results owns the collection, and filtering is consumer-owned by default. Modifier-Enter requires getSelectableItems, matching the oracle. Noninteractive results are keyboard-disabled intentionally; highlight reasons map native keyboard/pointer events rather than the full Base UI vocabulary. Popup focus explicitly returns to the opener and portal shells persist during hydration only.

Flow retains the pure layout and SVG routing algorithms but replaces motion/react with bounded native pointer-capture and wheel panning. Pan styling is local to the canvas. DOM-ordered registration supports keyed reorders and structural updates without requiring child rerenders. canvas=false disables pan/bounds behavior but retains the padded wrapper, and anchors affect horizontal connectors only, matching the pinned implementation.

ClipboardText owns a toast manager per instance instead of the oracle's shared global manager, routes anchored feedback and tooltips through KumoPortalProvider, and explicitly supplies tooltip role/description linkage missing from the native primitive. The shared copy helper verifies fallback success and unmount ignores pending clipboard completions. Clipboard animations exclude hover colors. Toast text is 14px, close controls have reserved space, and in-tree bump animation frames are cancelled on unmount.

ShikiProvider deduplicates equivalent language sets, resets loading/error state when reconfigured and disposes initialized and late-arriving engines. Language normalization rejects inherited object names. CodeHighlighted reveals copy controls on keyboard focus, uses the shared clipboard fallback helper and cancels/restarts its success timer. One-off server highlighting disposes in finally. Legacy Code.values remains ignored, as in the oracle.

CodeHighlighted reserves an intrinsic-width copy-control column for multi-line blocks instead of the oracle's absolute overlay, preventing buttons and success labels from obscuring source on narrow screens. Long lines remain horizontally scrollable inside their code viewport.

DatePicker uses @octanejs/day-picker 0.0.18 (v10 behavior) with native event/content/ref/component types and mapped initialFocus/fromMonth/toMonth/fromYear/toYear aliases. Removed deprecated class/style keys, components.Button and fromDate/toDate are not accepted; use current keys, specific buttons and hidden matchers. Navigation bounds expose aria-disabled rather than native disabled.

DateRangePicker normalizes navigation to the first of each month, ignores invalid month edits, emits local-midnight dates, removes unused duplicate IDs, and makes hover/focus color changes immediate. Its timezone remains display-only and SSR assumes matching initial local month and locale.

The standalone stylesheet export composes the pinned utility build and main component stylesheet because the pinned utility build omits .rdp calendar rules. All five oracle CSS copies retain their exact hashes.

Table.Header sticky positioning uses a header-wide z-2 stacking context rather than per-cell z-1. This corrects the oracle's pinned body cells painting over sticky header labels during two-axis scrolling.

Pagination initializes its input draft from the supplied page during SSR. Empty totals use a minimum maxPage of 1 and range 0-0; non-finite drafts restore the current page and fractional drafts truncate before clamping. Next/last controls disable at or beyond maxPage. Enter commits without submitting an enclosing form. These intentionally correct oracle edge cases; caller-owned page and perPage props must still be valid positive integers.
Handlers receive native DOM events rather than React synthetic events.
Refs use Octane ref-as-prop rather than React forwardRef.
Icon components and descriptors use @octanejs/phosphor-icons and Octane types.

Collapsible panels are kept mounted only during SSR hydration to avoid Octane's detached insertion-anchor failure when an initially closed Base UI disclosure first opens; normal post-hydration mounting behavior is preserved.

Dialog, Popover, and DropdownMenu portal shells are kept mounted only during SSR hydration to avoid Octane's detached insertion-anchor failure when an initially closed Base UI overlay first opens; popup content preserves normal post-hydration unmounting behavior.

Tabs implements native WAI-ARIA tab behavior at the Kumo boundary because @octanejs/base-ui 0.1.48 omits tab children from server output; the public Kumo controlled, uncontrolled, activation, rendering, overflow, and styling contracts are preserved.
Toolbar implements its native WAI-ARIA composite behavior at the Kumo boundary because @octanejs/base-ui 0.1.48 has no toolbar module.

Select, Autocomplete, and Combobox adapt Kumo's arbitrary values to @octanejs/aria collection keys. Kumo's side, align, offset, portal, and ordinary collision-flipping controls are mapped; Base UI-only anchor tracking, sticky positioning, alignItemWithTrigger, and advanced collision configuration remain accepted compatibility props without native behavior.

Select, Autocomplete, and Combobox keep an empty ARIA popover shell mounted only during SSR hydration to avoid Octane's detached insertion-anchor failure when an initially closed collection popup first opens; popup content preserves normal post-hydration mounting behavior.

Custom Autocomplete and Combobox filters receive values resolved from option text; distinct options with identical text cannot be distinguished by this ARIA filter adapter. Combobox.useFilter accepts multiple/value options but does not reproduce Base UI's selected-query browse exception. Positioning offsets currently accept numbers only and sides are physical rather than logical inline-start/inline-end.

Sidebar Content uses a plain overflow viewport because @octanejs/base-ui 0.1.48 has no scroll-area module; custom thumb and mask-fade are dropped while data-sidebar viewport attributes for scrollToItem are preserved.
The emergency octane-kumo/react compatibility subpath is not present because this slice has no irreducibly React-backed surface.
ssr: Toast/ClipboardText have real server compilation and trigger/copy node-adoption checks followed by toast dispatch/actions, tooltip description linkage and plain/anchored copy. Toast portal contents are client-created. Legacy Code/CodeBlock and the server trusted-HTML CodeBlock have real SSR and node-adoption checks. CodeHighlighted adopts escaped fallback and copy controls, then asynchronously highlights and copies after hydration. DatePicker (single, multiple and range), DateRangePicker, Table and Pagination, Button, Tooltip, Badge, Meter, SkeletonLine, Empty, Collapsible, Dialog, Popover, DropdownMenu, Input, InputArea, InputGroup, SensitiveInput, standalone and grouped Checkbox, Switch, and Radio, Select, Autocomplete, Combobox, Tabs, Toolbar, and MenuBar are covered for real server compilation, hydration node adoption, and post-hydration interaction. Broader component SSR and hydration remain unverified.
notes: The compatibility follow-up restores cn/safeRandomId, legacy InputGroup subpath exports/types, and Input/InputGroup.Input render composition. Select naming/spacing and its rapid keyboard-focus race are repaired, Flow geometry matches the oracle after restoring inherited line-height, and Switch layout/light off-state fill is corrected. The full follow-up differential records 84 runs and 162 checks, with only six shared Tooltip failures and six React-only command expectations failing. All 120 repeated Select keyboard cycles passed, and all 12 Select/Flow screenshot comparisons match at pixelmatch threshold 0.1 (nine decoded images are byte-identical). See audit/parity-report.md for remaining adaptations and original baseline findings; this is representative rather than exhaustive parity.

DeleteResource and CommandPalette have real SSR trigger-adoption checks followed by opening and confirmation/search/selection interactions; dialog content is client-created. Flow adopts server-rendered node DOM, hidden until client measurement establishes layout. No exhaustive hydration or React differential parity claim is made.

The composite slice tests resource confirmation, pending deletion and clipboard lifetimes, command value mapping/filtering/grouping/keyboard selection/portal routing, flow geometry/rounded paths/anchors/native ref composition/dynamic alignment and keyed node changes. The packed consumer compiles all three root/subpath exports and the native bundle graph remains React-free. These exports retain adapted-unverified status.

Chromium exercised command navigation/disabled skipping/Enter/modifier-Enter/filter-empty/Escape/focus restoration, confirmation copying/loading states, and dynamic horizontal/vertical flow layout with bounded mobile wheel/pointer panning. Light/dark, loading/empty and 390px mobile screenshots were inspected; content is readable and pages have no horizontal overflow. Flow intentionally clips offscreen nodes within its pannable canvas. Reproduce with tests/visual/command-palette.html, delete-resource.html and flow.html. Charts were excluded from this slice.

Toast/ClipboardText tests cover native root/subpath imports, typed manager options and actions in a packed consumer, five toast variants, hook/external dispatch, distinct duplicate semantics, custom content and promise outcomes, timeout lifecycle, portal precedence, clipboard sizes/ref/alternate text and labels, successful/failed fallback, repeated feedback, instance isolation and cleanup. Toasty.variant is accepted but unused as in the oracle. External managers do not queue before their provider subscribes. tests/visual/feedback.html is the reproducible theme-switching fixture. No exhaustive React differential parity is claimed.

Chromium exercised all five toast variants, Escape and swipe dismissal, actions, hover-paused timeout and stack expansion, keyboard clipboard copying, exact alternate clipboard values, tooltip description linkage, and repeated anchored feedback in light/dark themes. Expanded light, dark copied-feedback, and 390px mobile screenshots were inspected; feedback does not overlap adjacent fields and the mobile page has no horizontal overflow.

Chromium exercised code loading-to-ready, JavaScript/WASM engines, Tab focus and Enter/Space source copying in both themes, localized labels and fallback copying. Light/dark loading, ready/server HTML and 390px mobile screenshots were inspected. Mobile copy buttons do not overlap the code viewport and long lines scroll locally without page-wide overflow; platform overlay scrollbars may be hidden until scrolling.

The code slice covers legacy escaping/styles, client provider ownership and late disposal, aliases/fallback/errors, memoized highlighting, native copy controls and labels, real JavaScript/WASM engines, reusable server highlighting, and SSR/hydration. Packed consumers import root/legacy/client/server surfaces; bundled static code entry graphs contain no Shiki implementation and the entire native graph is React-free. Ordinary root component imports cannot reach Shiki, even dynamically. tests/visual/code.html reproduces light/dark themes, highlighted/numbered lines, long-line scrolling, fallback and server HTML rendering.

Date picking has repo-authored selection, native-event, bounds/focus alias, localization/customization, legacy month-edge, real SSR/hydration, root/subpath packed-consumer and React-free bundle checks. All six selection unions are compiled with required callback inference and negative native-event/type cases. No exhaustive React differential lane is claimed.

The date picker preview uses the public standalone stylesheet composition and includes light/dark single/multiple/range selections, disabled days, native month/year dropdowns, and all legacy sizes. Run tests/visual/date-pickers.html for reproducible review; the legacy month uses the local clock.

Chromium exercised both date-picker themes with ArrowRight focus and disabled-day skipping, Enter/Space selection/deselection, month navigation, multiple/range selection, month/year dropdown changes, and all legacy sizes with hover preview, keyboard selection and reset. Selected light/dark and 390px mobile screenshots were inspected; the page has no horizontal overflow, while wide legacy calendars scroll within their example containers.

The table/pagination browser fixture was exercised in Chromium for light/dark Space/Enter selection and navigation, bounded page input, Select End/Enter selection and focus restoration, popup appearance, pinned column/header hit-testing during two-axis scrolling, and a 390px viewport without page-wide horizontal overflow. Scroll viewports intentionally clip rows and let route text pass beneath opaque pinned cells.

Table and Pagination cover native compound APIs, refs and events, selection callbacks and aliases, controlled pages and internal drafts, known/unknown/empty totals, localized labels, page-size and page-number Select composition, and real SSR/hydration integration. The packed consumer exercises both root and component subpaths. tests/visual/table-pagination.html provides light/dark selectable resource tables with automatic/fixed layouts, compact/sticky headers and columns, both page selectors, and unknown/empty totals. These are repo-authored checks, not a React differential parity claim.
Button-family DOM behavior, native events, refs, loading transitions, icon forms, and tooltip trigger composition have repo-authored Octane tests.
Tooltip focus/Escape interaction, portal routing, hydration, and a browser-rendered open state have repo-authored Octane evidence.

Label, Field, and Input associations, native input events and refs, Base UI-style value details, validation precedence, password-manager attributes, and Input hydration have repo-authored Octane evidence.
InputArea and its Textarea alias cover native events and refs, Field associations, controlled and uncontrolled values, min/max row auto-resizing, cleanup, and hydration.

InputGroup covers the complete Input, Addon, Suffix, Button, Label, and Description compound surface; container, individual, and hybrid focus modes; inherited state and sizing; native refs and events; Field integration; and hydration.

SensitiveInput covers empty, masked, and revealed states; pointer and keyboard operation; controlled and uncontrolled values; native refs and form behavior; Clipboard API and fallback copying; accessible instructions and announcements; Field integration; and hydration.

Standalone Checkbox and the compound Group, Item, and Legend family cover native events and refs, controlled and uncontrolled state, label activation, form values, validation, accessibility associations, and hydration.

Standalone Switch and the compound Group, Item, and Legend family cover controlled and uncontrolled state, single label activation, refs, native form values, disabled and read-only behavior, accessible grouping, transitioning, semantic-token styling, and hydration.

The generic Radio and direct RadioGroup exports cover accessible naming, controlled and uncontrolled selection, native event details, roving keyboard focus, number and enum types, form serialization, group states, card appearance, and hydration.

Select, Autocomplete, and Combobox cover primitive and object values, controlled and uncontrolled state, single and multiple selection, disabled and read-only options, free-form and custom filtering, trigger render composition, chips, native collection keyboard behavior, portal routing, SSR/hydration, and representative visuals.

Badge, Meter, SkeletonLine, and Empty cover their Kumo variants, labels and values, SSR-stable seeded shimmer styles, flexible content, accessible command copying, semantic-token styling, and hydration.

The compound Collapsible family covers controlled and uncontrolled state, native event details, disabled behavior, render composition, state callbacks, refs, panel mounting, initially closed hydration, and representative visuals.

Dialog, Popover, and DropdownMenu preserve the React Kumo compound APIs, variants, portal-provider routing, render composition, controlled and uncontrolled state, native event details, focus and dismissal behavior, initially closed hydration, and representative open-state visuals.

Tabs, Toolbar, and MenuBar preserve the React Kumo public APIs and styling, with native value state, render composition, disabled handling, overflow behavior, roving keyboard focus, input cursor navigation, hydration, and representative visuals.
The package contract resolves root and component subpath imports, rejects React or ReactCompat imports in native source, and verifies the bundled native module graph remains React-free.

A temporary external consumer compiles Badge, Banner, Breadcrumbs, Button, CloudflareLogo, PoweredByCloudflare, Collapsible, Dialog, Popover, DropdownMenu, Select, Autocomplete, Combobox, Tabs, Toolbar, MenuBar, Empty, Grid/GridItem, Meter, SkeletonLine, Tooltip, Label, Field, Input, InputArea, Textarea, InputGroup, SensitiveInput, Checkbox, Switch, Text, Link, LayerCard, Surface, Sidebar, TableOfContents, and generic Radio APIs from the real packed tarball on every test run.
The upstream Kumo styles are shipped through stable export paths and guarded by exact SHA-256 source-copy checks.

Representative Button, Badge, Meter, SkeletonLine, Empty, Collapsible, Dialog, Popover, DropdownMenu, Select, Autocomplete, Combobox, Tabs, Toolbar, MenuBar, Tooltip, Input, InputArea, InputGroup, SensitiveInput, Checkbox, Switch, and Radio states have a reproducible light/dark visual fixture; overlay and selection popup states, navigation controls, Collapsible opening, and Empty and SensitiveInput copy interactions were manually exercised in that fixture.

LayerCard, Surface, Grid/GridItem, Text, Link, CloudflareLogo/PoweredByCloudflare, Banner, Breadcrumbs, TableOfContents, and Sidebar are Octane-native with variant contracts, compound APIs, and package-as-consumer type checks; tests/shell.test.tsx covers render composition, Banner Link identity, and Sidebar's provider/header/content/menu/footer smoke path.

The differential browser lane exercises Sidebar mobile opening and a menu action. Broader responsive behavior, peek, resize, and scrollToItem remain unverified. Its Content uses the accepted plain-overflow ScrollArea fallback described above.
Chart, SankeyChart, and TimeseriesChart are deferred at user request until needed, excluded from current parity and stable-release scope, and not counted as verified.

tests/parity/run.mjs compiles one shared fixture independently for the pinned React oracle and native Octane. The recorded 84 light/dark/mobile browser runs executed 156 assertions with 13 failures: six shared Tooltip semantic failures, six React-only command disabled-item expectations, and one intermittent native Select keyboard result that passed an unchanged focused repeat. Static API omissions, Select naming, Switch/Select/Flow visual drift, shared legacy-calendar overflow, adaptations and coverage limits are triaged in audit/parity-report.md and audit/parity-api.md. This is representative differential evidence, not clean or exhaustive parity; component statuses remain adapted-unverified.
